selection_basis: Performers who headlined romantic leads AND were themselves the subject of published appearance rankings, balanced by sex, spanning the 1980s to the 2020s. Chosen on that basis BEFORE any check of how easy each is to score, and before any pairing graph existed. This is a SEED, not the final cohort: scripts/identify_couples.py surfaces partners who are not on it, and those are added in later rounds.
known_limits: Anglophone and film-centric. Musicians and television-first performers enter only as discovered partners.
Nobody here was chosen because they would rank well. Tuning the cohort to produce a result is forbidden; see docs/SOURCE-HUNT.md.
scope: Films from 1980 onward. Stated as SCOPE, not hidden: the board covers the modern era and says so on the page.

rules.statement: TWO RULES DECIDE WHO APPEARS, and nobody is removed by hand. (1) Only films from 1980 on are graded. (2) A person needs at least 3 scored romances to be ranked. Everyone else stays in the data and still appears as a partner on other people's rows.
rules.why_no_hand_removals: An earlier version removed Audrey Hepburn, Sophia Loren, Paul Newman and Robert Redford by name, because their careers are mostly pre-1980. That worked but it was roster selection for presentation, which docs/SOURCE-HUNT.md warns against: the roster was chosen on prominence BEFORE anything was scored, deliberately. The two rules above reach a similar place without anyone choosing who. Measured with the 1980 floor: Hepburn has 1 post-1980 romance and is not ranked; Loren has 3, Newman 9 and Redford 16, and they are ranked on their post-1980 work. That is the honest consequence of the rule and it is preferred to picking names.
